random_subset.drawn_from: a seeded shuffle of the first 254 sampled roles (216 intern, 37 new grad, 1 junior)

held_out.drawn_from: 46 sampled roles never looked at while writing rules, 36 of which had description text. All are junior-labeled, because details were fetched in level order, so this is a harder slice and not a random hold-out.

conflict_calls.profile: An example profile, not a real person: would need sponsorship, enrolled in a bachelor's degree, graduating December 2027, returning to school, no full-time experience.

hard_cases.description: Hand-written cases for negation, preferred and alternative qualifications, boilerplate, conflicting text and missing profile facts. Reported apart from the random sample.

known_errors.what: A sentence about staff tenure ("42% of our employees have stayed for 10+ years") was read as a 10-year experience floor.
"Home office is available up to 2 days per week" was read as two days in the office.
"Active TS/SCI clearance ... and eligibility for clearance crossover" was labeled as clearance eligibility when it asks for an active clearance.
"We don't specifically look for those working towards a computer science degree" was read as a must-be-a-student line.
"Recently graduated or currently enrolled" was summarized as students only.
A role in Bangalore that mentioned the U.S. in passing got a U.S. sponsorship comparison.
"Not eligible for new H-1B sponsorship" was treated as no sponsorship of any kind.
known_errors.status: Fixed in 0.2.0. It now reads as needs clarification.

known_errors.what: "1 to 3 years, or an equivalent combination of education and experience" was treated as a hard floor.
known_errors.status: Fixed in 0.2.0. It now reads as one of several options.

known_errors.what: Pay stated as one figure in a sentence ("the annual salary expectation is around $50,760") was missed.
When a listing gives both a base range and a total compensation range, the first one found is shown.
Sponsorship policies written as a paragraph of legal context, with no clear yes or no, are not picked up.
Listings not written in English are mostly unread.

caveats: The fixes in 0.2.0 were made after the checks above and have not been re-checked on roles the rules have never seen.
The conflict calls were reviewed on the same sample the rules were tuned on.
27 of the 300 sampled roles had no description text on the board, so nothing could be read.
